title: Is this Chinese Titanium frameset worth a look? Hi Light G7.2 Titanium Gravel Bike

takeaways.text: Built with GRX shifters, a 46/34 crank, 11–42 cassette and DT Swiss wheels, the complete bike weighed about 10 kg; his attempt to weigh the bare frame alone was not legible.
Kenda Flintridge Pro 700×40 tires measuring about 43–44 mm leave plenty of room against the 45 mm rating; he guesses 50 mm might fit but has not tried.
The frame routes fully internally; with a conventional stem the hoses enter at the headset, which his mechanic found acceptable.
Long trail makes it stable and comfortable rather than twitchy, snappy enough on the road, composed on rocky descents and with little or no toe overlap; not a race bike.
He says the frameset costs about a third of the ₱100,000–150,000 he saw for other titanium framesets in the Philippines.

disclosure: The Philippine distributor sent the frameset so the presenter's shop could build a display bike and sell the brand; the video has an unrelated coffee sponsor.
summary: A Philippine shop owner's Hi-Light G7.2 titanium gravel frameset built with parts from his old bike, with road and off-road ride impressions.
